page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by 8.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2923.48. However, multi-core and memory performance are constrained. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the 2-vCPU limit. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 136.13 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 24.26 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

The c2d-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point into Google Cloud's compute-optimized family, providing dedicated AMD EPYC cores without the higher cost of larger instances. The primary tradeoff is the low resource density, which limits throughput in multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and database operations. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development or testing workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation but do not require high memory bandwidth or local storage.
